Systems utilizing loop equations were discussed at the 19th AIVC Conference on Ventilation Technologies in Urban Areas, held in Oslo, Norway, from September 28–30, 1998, with findings published on pages 47–56. 2. Fanger P. conducted an analysis of thermal comfort and its applications in environmental engineering, detailed in the book published by McGraw-Hill, New York, in 1970. 3. Brady MT, Evans J, and Cuartas J. studied the survival and disinfection of parainfluenza viruses on environmental surfaces, with their findings published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 1990 (Volume 18, Issue 1, pages 18–23). 4. Suarez DL, Spackman E, Senne DA, Bulaga L, Welsch AC, and Froberg K. examined the effects of various disinfectants on the detection of avian influenza virus using real-time RT-PCR, with results published in Avian Diseases in 2003 (Volume 47, Supplement 3, pages 1091–1095). 5. Sattar SA, Jacobsen H, Springthorpe VS, Cusack TM, and Rubino JR. investigated chemical disinfection to prevent the transfer of rhinovirus type 14 from environmental surfaces to hands, with their study published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology in 1993 (Volume 59, Issue 5, pages 1579–1585). 6. Sattar SA, Springthorpe VS, Karim Y, and Loro P. evaluated the chemical disinfection of non-porous surfaces experimentally contaminated with four human pathogenic viruses, with findings published in Epidemiology and Infection in 1989 (Volume 102, Issue 3, pages 493–505). 7. Rabenau HF, Kampf G, Cinatl J, and Doerr HW. assessed the efficacy of various disinfectants against the SARS coronavirus, with results published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 2005 (Volume 61, Issue 2, pages 107–111). 8. Dettenkofer M, Wenzler S, Amthor S, Antes G, Motschall E, and Daschner FD. conducted a systematic review to determine whether disinfection of environmental surfaces influences nosocomial infection rates, with findings published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 2004 (Volume 32, Issue 2, pages 84–89). 9. Scott E and Bloomfield SF. investigated the effectiveness of detergent washing, drying, and chemical disinfection on the contamination of cleaning cloths, with their study published in Journal of Applied Bacteriology in 1990 (Volume 68, Issue 3, pages 279–283). 10. Medcraft JW, Hawkins JM, Fletcher BN, and Dadswell JV. explored the potential hazards of spray cleaning hospital ward floors, with findings published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 1987 (Volume 9, Issue 2, pages 151–157). 11. Spaulding EH. discussed chemical disinfection of medical and surgical materials in the book Disinfection, Sterilization, and Preservation, edited by Block S, published by Lea & Febiger, Philadelphia, in 1968 (pages 517–531). 12. Rutala WA. authored the APIC guideline for selecting and using disinfectants, published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 1996 (Volume 24, Issue 4, pages 313–342). 13. The World Health Organization (WHO) released interim guidelines on infection prevention and control of epidemicand pandemic-prone acute respiratory diseases in healthcare settings. 14. Cefai C, Richards J, Gould FK, and McPeake P. reported an outbreak of Acinetobacter respiratory tract infections caused by incomplete disinfection of ventilatory equipment, published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 1990 (Volume 15, Issue 2, pages 177–182). 15. Craven DE, Lichtenberg DA, Goularte TA, Make BJ, and McCabe WR. identified contaminated medication nebulizers in mechanical ventilator circuits as a source of bacterial aerosols, with findings published in the American Journal of Medicine in 1984 (Volume 77, Issue 5, pages 834–838). 16. Spach DH, Silverstein FE, and Stamm WE. reviewed the transmission of infections via gastrointestinal endoscopy and bronchoscopy, with their study published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 1993 (Volume 118, Issue 2, pages 117–128). 17. Weber DJ and Rutala WA. analyzed lessons from outbreaks associated with bronchoscopy, with findings published in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2001 (Volume 22, Issue 7, pages 403–408). 18. Wheeler PW, Lancaster D, and Kaiser AB. investigated bronchopulmonary cross-colonization and infections related to mycobacterial contamination of bronchoscope suction valves, with results published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1989 (Volume 159, Issue 5, pages 954–958). 19. Poledore AP. studied the sanitizing efficiency of dishwashing machines, with findings published in the Journal of Foodservice in 1980 (pages 17–25). 20. Stahl Wernersson E, Johansson E, and Hakanson H. examined cross-contamination in dishwashers, with results published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 2004 (Volume 56, Issue 4, pages 312–317). 21. Ijaz MK, Sattar SA, Johnson-Lussenburg CM, Springthorpe VS, and Nair RC. evaluated the effects of relative humidity, atmospheric temperature, and suspending medium on the airborne survival of human rotavirus, with findings published in Canadian Journal of Microbiology in 1985 (Volume 31, Issue 8, pages 681–685). 22. Marks PJ, Vipond IB, Carlisle D, Deakin D, Fey RE, and Caul EO. provided evidence for airborne transmission of Norwalk-like virus in a hotel restaurant, with findings published in Epidemiology and Infection in 2000 (Volume 124, Issue 3, pages 481–487). 23. Marks PJ, Vipond IB, Regan FM, Wedgwood K, Fey RE, and Caul EO. documented a school outbreak of Norwalk-like virus, providing evidence for airborne transmission, with findings published in Epidemiology and Infection in 2003 (Volume 131, Issue 1, pages 727–736). 24. Battles DR and Vesley D. studied the relationship between wash water temperature and sanitation in hospital laundry, with findings published in the Journal of Environmental Health in 1981 (Volume 43, Issue 5, pages 244–250). 25. Blaser MJ, Smith PF, Cody HJ, Wang WL, and LaForce FM. investigated the killing of fabric-associated bacteria in hospital laundry using low-temperature washing, with findings published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1984 (Volume 149, Issue 1, pages 48–57). 26. Christian RR, Manchester JT, and Mellor MT. assessed the bacteriological quality of fabrics washed at lower-than-standard temperatures in hospital laundry facilities, with findings published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology in 1983 (Volume 45, Issue 2, pages 591–597). 27. Barker J and Jones MV. explored the potential spread of infection caused by aerosol contamination of surfaces after flushing a domestic toilet, with findings published in Journal of Applied Microbiology in 2005 (Volume 99, Issue 2, pages 339–347). 28. Morawska L. examined the fate of droplets in indoor environments and the potential to prevent the spread of infection, with findings published in Indoor Air in 2006 (Volume 16, Issue 5, pages 335–347). 29. Karanfil LV, Conlon M, Lykens K, et al. studied methods to reduce nosocomially transmitted respiratory syncytial virus, with findings published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 1999 (Volume 27, Issue 2, pages 91–96). 30. Mlinaric-Galinovic G and Varda-Brkic D. reported on nosocomial respiratory syncytial virus infections in children's wards, with findings published in Diagnostic Microbiology and Infectious Disease in 2000 (Volume 37, Issue 4, pages 237–246). 31. Thorburn K, Kerr S, Taylor N, and van Saene HK. documented an RSV outbreak in a pediatric intensive care unit, with findings published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 2004 (Volume 57, Issue 3, pages 194–201). 32. Ibricevic A, Pekosz A, Walter MJ, et al. studied influenza virus receptor specificity and cell tropism in mouse and human airway epithelial cells, with findings published in Journal of Virology in 2006 (Volume 80, Issue 15, pages 7469–7480). 33. The CDC published guidelines for preventing the transmission of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in healthcare facilities in 1994, with updates in 2005. 34. Le DH, Bloom SA, Nguyen QH, et al. reported a lack of SARS transmission among public hospital workers in Vietnam, with findings published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2004 (Volume 10, Issue 2, pages 265–268). 35. Park BJ, Peck AJ, Kuehner MJ, et al. documented a lack of SARS transmission among healthcare workers in the United States, with findings published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2004 (Volume 10, Issue 2, pages 244–248). 36. Peck AJ, Newbern EC, Feikin DR, et al. studied SARS case-patients, with findings published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2004 (Volume 10, Issue 2, pages 217–224). 37. Ali Y, Dolan M, Fendler E, and Larson E. reviewed the use of alcohols in disinfection, as detailed in the book Disinfection, Sterilization, and Preservation, 5th edition, edited by Block S, published by Williams and Wilkins in 2000 (pages 229–253). 38. Bell DM. analyzed public health interventions and the spread of SARS in 2003, with findings published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2004 (Volume 10, Issue 11, pages 1900–1906). 39. Rutala WA, Weber DJ, Gergen MF, and Gratta AR. evaluated the efficacy of a washer-pasteurizer for disinfecting respiratory-care equipment, with findings published in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2000 (Volume 21, Issue 5, pages 333–336). 40. Gillis J and Rennick J. emphasized affirming parental love in the pediatric intensive care unit, with findings published in Pediatric Critical Care Medicine in 2006 (Volume 7, Issue 2, pages 165–168). 41. Leidy NK, Margolis MK, Marcin JP, et al. studied the impact of severe respiratory syncytial virus on children, caregivers, and families during hospitalization and recovery, with findings published in Pediatrics in 2005 (Volume 115, Issue 6, pages 1536–1546). 42. Hanrahan KS and Lofgren M. examined the risks associated with toys in the microenvironment of infants in neonatal intensive care units, with findings published in Advances in Neonatal Care in 2004 (Volume 4, Issue 4, pages 184–201). 43. Avila-Aguero ML, German G, Paris MM, and Herrera JF. investigated whether toys in pediatric hospitals serve as bacterial sources, with findings published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 2004 (Volume 32, Issue 5, pages 287–290). 44. Buttery JP, Alabaster SJ, Heine RG, et al. reported a multiresistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa outbreak in a pediatric oncology ward linked to bath toys, with findings published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 1998 (Volume 17, Issue 6, pages 509–513). 45. Davies MW, Mehr S, Garland ST, and Morley CJ. studied bacterial colonization of toys in neonatal intensive care cots, with findings published in Pediatrics in 2000 (Volume 106, Issue 2, Article E18). 46. Hick JL, Hanfling D, Burstein JL, et al. discussed healthcare facility and community strategies for patient care surge capacity, with findings published in Annals of Emergency Medicine in 2004 (Volume 44, Issue 3, pages 253–261). 47. Hogg W, Lemelin J, Huston P, and Dahrouge S. explored increasing epidemic surge capacity through home-based hospital care, with findings published in Canadian Family Physician in 2006 (Volume 52, pages 563–564, 570–572). 48. Martin SD. addressed concerns about avian flu in home healthcare, with findings published in Home Healthcare Nurse in 2006 (Volume 24, Issue 1, pages 38–45).
